## Prerequisites:
First download both the image.jpg and flag.enc files from the challenge

Then use exiftool to find the metadata in the image file
```bash
┌──(tanush㉿kali)-[~/Downloads]
└─$ exiftool image.jpg
ExifTool Version Number         : 13.50
File Name                       : image.jpg
Directory                       : .
File Size                       : 21 kB
File Modification Date/Time     : 2026:07:04 07:36:19+00:00
File Access Date/Time           : 2026:07:04 07:40:23+00:00
File Inode Change Date/Time     : 2026:07:04 07:36:19+00:00
File Permissions                : -rw-rw-r--
File Type                       : JPEG
File Type Extension             : jpg
MIME Type                       : image/jpeg
JFIF Version                    : 1.01
Resolution Unit                 : None
X Resolution                    : 1
Y Resolution                    : 1
Comment                         : 
Image Width                     : 512
Image Height                    : 512
Encoding Process                : Baseline DCT, Huffman coding
Bits Per Sample                 : 8
Color Components                : 3
Y Cb Cr Sub Sampling            : YCbCr4:2:0 (2 2)
Image Size                      : 512x512
Megapixels                      : 0.262

```
the comment field contains a long hex string which can be a secret, so we convert it into a key file.

```bash
┌──(tanush㉿kali)-[~/Downloads]
└─$ exiftool -Comment -b image.jpg | xxd -r -p > key.pem
```
then we check if the recovered key is valid or not.
```bash

└─$ cat key.pem

┌──(tanush㉿kali)-[~/Downloads]
└─$ openssl rsa -in key.pem -check -noout
RSA key ok
```
then we try to decrypt the flag from recovered private key
```bash
┌──(tanush㉿kali)-[~/Downloads]
└─$ openssl pkeyutl -decrypt -inkey key.pem -in flag.enc -out flag.txt
```

picoCTF{rs4_k3y_1n_1mg_66388eb3}
